bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing By Maria Dsouza October 30, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a Rs 2,014 crore drinking water project for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri, with Rs 1,774 crore approved by NABARD to upgrade water infrastructure under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. The scheme will use surface water from the Sone river to strengthen existing supply systems in the three towns. The announcement was made by the chief minister on Thursday, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. Choudhary said the project would expand drinking water facilities and improve water availability in the three areas. The state government said the scheme would initially serve a population of around 8 lakh. The project is expected to cover nearly 12 lakh people by 2051, indicating that the planned infrastructure is being designed around long-term population growth in the three towns. The announcement did not provide details of the proposed treatment capacity, distribution network, construction schedule, tendering process or commissioning date. The funding approved by NABARD is part of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, which supports infrastructure projects through institutional financing. The statement did not specify how the remaining amount from the total project cost would be financed or provide a town-wise allocation for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri. The proposed use of Sone river water will reinforce existing drinking water systems rather than replace them, according to the chief minister’s statement. The announcement therefore links the project to both source augmentation and the strengthening of civic supply infrastructure. Details on water treatment facilities, transmission lines, storage arrangements and household-level connections were not included in the information released. Choudhary also linked the initiative to Bihar’s Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign, which promotes water conservation, environmental protection and the sustainable use of water resources. The project’s stated objective is to provide residents with clean and adequate drinking water while expanding the capacity of urban and surrounding supply systems. The announcement places the three towns within a wider state effort to improve basic infrastructure with support from the Union government and financial institutions. For residents, the eventual impact will depend on how quickly the approved funding is converted into construction, treatment and distribution capacity, as well as how the expanded network is operated and maintained. The Bihar government has not yet announced the project’s implementation timeline, construction milestones or completion date. Further details are expected as the scheme moves from funding approval to execution. The project is expected to serve around 8 lakh people initially and nearly 12 lakh by 2051. The Chief Minister’s Office said on Thursday that NABARD had approved Rs 1,774 crore for upgrading Bihar’s drinking water infrastructure under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF). The remaining components of the Rs 2,014 crore investment were not detailed in the statement. The project will draw surface water from the Sone river to reinforce existing drinking water systems in Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri. The announcement did not specify the planned treatment capacity, distribution network length, construction schedule or the individual allocation for each town. Choudhary thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government for supporting the project through the financing approval. According to the statement, the state government considers the scheme part of its broader effort to expand basic infrastructure and improve civic amenities across Bihar. The proposed coverage numbers indicate that the scheme has been planned around both current demand and long-term population growth. The three towns together are expected to see the number of people covered rise from approximately 8 lakh at present to nearly 12 lakh by 2051. The statement did not provide a projected date for commissioning the system or details of the phases in which the network will be developed. The use of Sone river water will add a surface-water source to the towns’ existing supply arrangements. The announcement described the project as a measure to improve water availability, but did not set out the present reliability of supplies, the condition of existing infrastructure or the treatment and transmission systems that will be upgraded. The Chief Minister also linked the initiative to the Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign, which focuses on water conservation, environmental protection and the sustainable use of water resources. The statement presented the drinking water project as part of that wider approach to managing water and expanding access to basic services. NABARD’s approval under RIDF provides the principal financing commitment disclosed so far. The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund is being used in this case to support drinking water infrastructure, while implementation will be undertaken by the Bihar government. The supplied announcement did not identify the executing agency, procurement process, land requirements or safeguards connected with drawing water from the Sone. The state government said it remained committed to ensuring that residents had access to clean and adequate drinking water. The next publicly stated step is the implementation of the approved project, although the announcement did not provide a tender deadline, construction timetable or commissioning milestone. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat, beginning today. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 14 thousand crore rupees in Banaskantha today. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). He will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to 19 thousand crore rupees. He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskantha. The Centre will strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10 to 20 times. Thereafter, the Prime Minister will travel to Ekta Nagar, Kevadia and inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026. Tomorrow, Prime Minister Modi will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over four hundred crore rupees in Ekta Nagar. The projects include a sewage and water treatment plant, facade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat, and the Rainforest, among others. The Prime Minister will also participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

national_raw_news.title: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang ANI | Updated: Oct 30, 2026 03:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 30 (ANI): The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, commenced on Thursday at Tawang , Arunachal Pradesh . The three-day Mart, being held from October 29 to 31, aims to showcase the tourism potential of the eight North Eastern States and strengthen business engagement with domestic and international tourism markets. The inaugural session was held in the presence of Gajendra Singh Shekhawat , Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER); Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh ; and Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim. Tourism Ministers from the North Eastern States, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, international and domestic tourism stakeholders and representatives of the travel industry were also present. Addressing the inaugural session, Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat emphasised that the International Tourism Mart has evolved beyond a promotional platform into an important avenue for tourism partnerships and business opportunities. He stated, “ITM is not merely a tourism marketplace; it is a platform for building partnerships, generating business opportunities and creating a shared vision for the growth of tourism in the North East Region.” Highlighting the immense potential of the region, the Minister said that its rich biodiversity, cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and natural landscapes offer distinctive opportunities for adventure, nature-based and experiential tourism. He particularly emphasised the potential of adventure tourism, music festivals and concert tourism to attract new visitor segments, encourage longer stays and generate economic opportunities for local communities. He also called for developing tourism experiences with appropriate safety standards, community participation and environmental safeguards. The Minister highlighted the Government’s continued focus on improving connectivity, tourism infrastructure and destination experiences in the North Eastern Region. He also underlined the Ministry’s support for tourism promotion through domestic and international travel fairs, festivals, digital platforms and familiarisation visits, along with skill development initiatives to create employment opportunities for local youth. national_raw_news.content: India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India | Business About Career Advertisement Media Partnership Contact Us HOME NEWS RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS SUBMIT PRESS RELEASE NEWS DESK RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS INTERVIEW Home News Law & Governance Article India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST Senior officials from the Department of Posts and UTI AMC during the meeting at UTI AMC’s Corporate Office (Photo/PIB). Image Credit: ANI SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. According to a release issued by the Ministry of Communications on Thursday, the expanded collaboration aims to simplify investor verification, improve access to mutual fund services and strengthen financial inclusion. "Under the Pan-India KYC Verification Project, India Post will leverage its extensive postal network and last-mile connectivity to facilitate Know Your Customer (KYC) verification at investors' doorsteps, including in remote and underserved areas," the ministry said. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) extending the existing agreement was signed by Adnan Ahmed, Chief General Manager, Parcel & CCS Directorate, Department of Posts, and Vetri Subramaniam, Managing Director and CEO of UTI Asset Management Company Limited, in Mumbai on Thursday. The expanded partnership builds on an earlier KYC remediation initiative that helped investors complete pending verification requirements and address documentation gaps. "Building on the earlier KYC remediation initiative, which helped investors complete pending KYC requirements, improve compliance and address documentation gaps, the expanded collaboration is expected to strengthen investor servicing, encourage wider participation in mutual funds and support uninterrupted access to mutual fund investments," the release stated. India Post has already been providing doorstep KYC verification services for mutual fund investors. According to an earlier Ministry of Communications release issued in April 2025, India Post had completed over 5 lakh KYC verifications for UTI and the Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India (SUUTI). The Department of Posts subsequently signed similar agreements with Nippon India Mutual Fund in April 2025 and SBI Mutual Fund later that month. In July 2025, India Post also entered into an agreement with the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) to facilitate KYC verification for mutual fund investors through its network of over 1.64 lakh post offices.
